decisions.reason: The candidate already records the 4 Small Block and 3 Big Block tickets issued per coded-referral mint. Changing their post-issuance lifecycle does not alter issuance quantity or recipient.

The same-message introduction already records the required two ticket counters and permanent badges. Resetting the underlying counters after draws does not change which metadata fields must be visible.

The candidate's prize amount, winner count, weighted-ticket eligibility, pool trigger, and royalty funding remain valid. The narrower validity and reset rules for Small Block Tickets are independently represented by the source Requirement.
The candidate's winner count, prize amount, pool target, and draw condition remain unchanged. Big Block ticket validity and post-draw reset are independently owned by the source Requirement.
The client explicitly preserves allocation of one ticket to a random existing NFT when no referral code is used. The lifecycle adjustment does not change that allocation rule.
The client explicitly states that prize claims remain manual, so the ticket-lifecycle adjustment does not change the claim flow.
The client preserves the rule that secondary royalties fund prize pools without creating tickets. Ticket expiration and reset behavior do not alter that rule.
The client explicitly states that the $10 commission remains automatic, so the ticket-lifecycle adjustment does not change commission amount or distribution.
The ticket-lifecycle decision has no semantic effect on the current or planned product names.
